title: Bengal in 1756–1757: A Selection of Public and Private Papers Dealing with the Affairs of the British in Bengal during the Reign of Siraj-Uddaula, with Notes and an Historical Introduction, Volume II
note: Edited by S. C. Hill and published in London by John Murray in 1905 as part of the Indian Records Series. The volume reproduces public and private papers concerning British affairs in Bengal under Siraj-ud-Daulah, with Hill's notes and historical introduction. Bibliographic details verified against the title page and Internet Archive catalog record.
subcategory: East India Company papers and correspondence
whyItMatters: The volume preserves Company correspondence and contemporary papers that document the fall of Calcutta and the later political use of the episode. Hill's editorial framing is an early twentieth-century colonial history and should be distinguished from the documents he reprints.
